items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889; Gideon president 1889-1911; creamery 1891 (story 1).
Article VII: paid by butterfat by test, not weight; 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern'.
'Under payment by weight a short pipette would have cost nobody anything.'
Effie Loomis secretary 1901-1940, Teague bookkeeper 1905-1945, Sill buttermaker.
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager from 1913; nephew rejected.
Story 8: yearly 'station gain' line, five and a quarter per cent, carried to general account, already 'as usual' in 1898.
Station 7 miles up valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, 1896 glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighed in, composite jars, fixed 17.6 c.c. charge, neck graduated for full charge, cream to Larrow Green.
Ammon & Sons Tarnet invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
Invoice table: 6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., bottles, acid measure, tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 6: 'The gap was a flat 0.19, the same in July as in February'; story 2: 3.61 +/-0.03 wet years and dry.
Section A never says the pipette cannot be checked without a burette, none in the county; the uncheckable-instrument point appears only in Section F.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, tester twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925 (1895 'went up' handled under deductions).
Routine described; book in his own hand, five columns, errors crossed out and initialled.
1896 3.80 on borrowed glass; 3.61 +/-0.03 from 1898.
8 May-10 July 1911, borrowed measure, 3.80, back on 10 July, '?' against it.
Orra Brant, Emmet's younger sister; tester married to sister of the patron who lost most.

1919 circular signed by Vose; 17 March 1925 statement that he could not say why the figures were what they were and never took cream (the 'tested as taught' wording is absent but the core statement is there).
Died February 1934 uncleared; book impounded March 1925, Historical Rooms since 1959.
Hessel Bottom wet meadow, six farms, Emmet Brant's largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; weights always agreed.
Complaints from about 1902; Hollow-vs-Green gap given as 0.17 against Larrow Green's 3.78, kept separate from the 0.19.
Grigg committee sampled Jan-Mar 1908, blamed the hay, reported as its finding.
1910 leaf 200,000 lb on 3.42; story 3 says the error is 'in proportion to the milk's richness'.
Roy kept it from 1929, lent it to Ivy in 1958; Hazel after 1962.
Alder Corners, Vessey County, over Redlow Ridge, Jerome Cudd; opened first season 1914.
From 1915 four Bottom men hauled summer milk over the ridge, station the rest of the year.
Own new glass; compared his figures with no one's; Vessey County; 'independent control on different glass'.
'In every overlap season the same cows' summer milk tested 3.80 over the ridge and 3.61 at the station, a gap of 0.19'; sixteen seasons 1915-1930 of hauling stated.
Same men's midsummer milk tested differently; defeats both hay and water.
Rosalie, his daughter, took over 1941 and copied the figures for Ivy in 1958 (sixteen-season table given).
Strawn, Ordell circuit 1907-March 1936, notebook every year, kin to nobody.
Lactometer at each visit; never found water at the station.
12 June 1923, against a burette, 'Condemned the lot, the whole crate.'
Never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Order 28 June, acknowledged 2 July, in use July; 1924 3.80, station stayed ~3.80 after 1923.
Crate to loft over intake room; notebooks to state office 1936, Farland library 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition January 1925.
Frick board 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); none established.
'Four books and nothing else' incl. Strawn's 1923 notebook (exhibit 4, holding the condemnation); nobody laid them side by side.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, no finding; 4 May award $3,800 'without admission', charged to station account.
Gives one-fifth of $19,000 but never says the award was charged to the account into which the loss had accumulated as 'gain' (the run says the gain went to the general account).
Ivy b. 1931, Duncan's daughter / Orra's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland; Vaught of the State Agricultural College.
Section A never states that Ivy assembled records never before in the same room; that synthesis appears only in Section G.
February 1958, crate in the loft, nine survived.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.88 short, 95%.
One part in twenty low from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923; 3.61 vs 3.80, 0.19.
40M lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 present, but Section A never states that 76,000 lb equals the sum of the station-gain entries; only the 1898 single entry is given.
Bulletin 471 October 1958; 35 years after condemnation, 33 after dismissal, 24 after death.
Granddaughter.
Duncan son of Ansel, Ivy daughter of Duncan.
Second cousins with correct derivation.
'so I take full' and says a half-sister would make them 'half second cousins', which contradicts the key's point that it does not change the answer; E#35 resolves 'Full'.
Gideon Vose, son not nephew.
Gideon drafted Article VII, which made the station test final; Selby defended his father's rule.
'nothing supports one, and I answer: none' is a definite assertion.
Treats the family member's denial as decisive rather than noting that a denial is not a record; the item is void under the key's assertion rule.
0.95, 5% low, one part in twenty.
76,000; 5.00% of delivered, 5.26% of credited, denominators named.
$77.93 with sum.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 y 1 m 11 d (~26 y 6 w) vs 25 full years 1898-1922; part years excluded.
Abstains: 1896 intake cannot be determined.
Variable: the pipette, 8 May-10 July.
Tester, bottles, acid, hand tester, scale, patrons, herds, hay held constant.
3.80 for nine weeks, 3.61 again on 10 July.
Cause in the glass, water/theft/hay ruled out; limits: size per pipette, source of the measure.
Ledger/Sill, 1911 book, Strawn, Alder Corners, each attributed to a narrator.
Independence argued; ledger and 1911 would stand without the 1958 measurement.
A09: whether the 1916 conversation happened 'cannot be settled'; Teague vs Kyle given.
Yes, knew tests ran low: 1919 circular, complaints since 1902.
Manager from 1913, signed the station-gain sheets, 1919 circular.
A03 abstained ('cannot be determined'); signing vs reading, and no source showing he connected the line (borderline on the two observations).
1924 average 3.80 (doc), weigh book 1897 (doc), six farms, crate in loft, Selby 1913, all resolved with methods.
Pair table: 16.27 (arith), 12 July (28 June order), $77.39 (sum), and more.
A04 (works books burned 1931), A06 (ND with date note), A10 (undated by-laws, lost minute book).
r15, r18, r20, r07, r05, r03 self-refutations identified.
16.72/17.6 = 0.95, proportional 0.19 on 3.80, onset 1897 / cessation 1923 with nothing else changing.
Water (Vose, Sill) defeated by Strawn's lactometer, Alder Corners.
Theft (Teague) defeated by the heavy cream in the ledger, 1911, 1924.
Hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter / nil summer against a flat gap.
A07: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glass? No.' A headline verdict, not an abstention.
A05: 'This cannot be determined.'
About 143 words.
Test book, weigh book, Strawn's notebook, ledger, Alder Corners tests, invoice.
Decoys attributed as blame, no wrong headline figures.

Gullibility A08: E#35 '-> Full, by the two nearest witnesses' (and B2 'I take full') resolves full vs half sibling
Gullibility A01: B4 'I answer: none' on Vose-Keddie kinship
Gullibility A07: F5 'No.' on whether the board examined the glass
